les: Baie mense op een plek, en nie almal gelyk nie
kaps_punt: Mapungubwe: eerste staat in Suider-Afrika 1220 - 1300: Eerste dorp; Duidelike sosiale klasse

items.bewering: In 'n klein nedersetting het die meeste gesinne self hulle kos verbou en hulle diere aangehou.
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Mapungubwe' (worldhistory.org/Mapungubwe): the people of the region were agro-pastoralists who grew millet and sorghum and herded cattle, sheep and goats. The Met essay 'Mapungubwe (ca. 1050-1270)' describes long-standing regional networks moving cattle and other goods before Mapungubwe. 'Die meeste' is a properly limited quantifier.

items.bewering: By Mapungubwe het baie meer mense saam op een plek gewoon as in 'n klein nedersetting.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Kingdom of Mapungubwe': 'The capital's population was 5,000 by 1250', with settlements all round the hill. The Met essay also gives a population of up to about 5 000. The lesson gives no number, only the comparison, and the comparison holds.

items.bewering: Party van die mense het nie self hulle kos verbou of diere aangehou nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Kingdom of Mapungubwe': the elite lived on the hilltop and wealth came in as tribute 'paid in crops, animals'; population growth 'may have led to full-time specialists in ceramics'. The Met essay contrasts the elite's homes, diet and burials with those of the commoners. 'Party' is a properly limited quantifier.

items.bewering: Een leier het vir die hele dorp en al die mense daar besluit.
items.bron: Zimbabwe Field Guide, 'An Introduction to the significance of Mapungubwe': rulers who isolated themselves from ordinary people through sacred leadership, with the ruler on the hill. Wikipedia, 'Kingdom of Mapungubwe': 'The leader and elites inhabited the hilltop.' Huffman (J. Anthropological Archaeology 2009) describes sacred leadership centred on one king.

items.bewering: Kos is ook van buite die dorp ingebring. Ander nedersettings het oeste en vee aan die koning gegee.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Kingdom of Mapungubwe': 'A large amount of wealth was accumulated via tributes, which were paid in crops, animals, and sometimes rarer goods'; the same article describes a tiered settlement hierarchy below the capital.

items.bewering: Mapungubwe was een van die eerste dorpe in Suider-Afrika.
items.blok: Een van die eerste dorpe in Suider-Afrika
items.bron: The Met essay calls Mapungubwe the earliest known site in southern Africa where leaders were spatially separated from their followers, and a city and trading centre from 1220. The softened form 'een van die eerste' is the correct one: Chirikure et al. 2014 (PLoS ONE 9(10): e111224, 'Zimbabwe Culture before Mapungubwe: New Evidence from Mapela Hill') show stone-walled terraces and class distinction at Mapela Hill, about 90 km north-west, from the 11th century, about two centuries before Mapungubwe Hill. Wikipedia notes that 'first state' was a traditional assumption. The bare 'Eerste dorp' and 'eerste staat' appear only in the copied CAPS bullet, not in the lesson text, and the lesson should keep it that way.

items.bewering: Van 1220 tot 1300 was die dorp die hoofstad van 'n koninkryk.
items.blok: Een van die eerste dorpe in Suider-Afrika
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Kingdom of Mapungubwe': 'Around 1220 ... the Mapungubwe elite moved to settle the top of Mapungubwe Hill', and the population moved away 'around 1300'. The Met essay gives 1220 to 1290/1300 for the city and trading-centre phase. SAHO ('Mapungubwe') gives about 1200 to 1300. These dates match the CAPS heading. Some sources end the period at 1290 rather than 1300, but that is ordinary variation in dating and does not make the claim false.

items.bewering: Mapungubwe het in die Limpopo-vallei gelê.
items.blok: Een van die eerste dorpe in Suider-Afrika
items.bron: SAHO, 'Mapungubwe' (sahistory.org.za/article/mapungubwe): on the border of South Africa, Zimbabwe and Botswana, near the confluence of the Limpopo and Shashe rivers.

items.bewering: Die koning en sy naaste familie het bo-op die Mapungubwe-heuwel gewoon.
items.blok: Nie almal het dieselfde geleef nie
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Kingdom of Mapungubwe': 'The leader and elites inhabited the hilltop, with the population below.' The Met essay places an elite graveyard on top of the hill. Zimbabwe Field Guide: rulers living on the hill, the common people on the plains below.

items.bewering: Ander mense het namens die koning gelei en hom raad gegee.
items.blok: Nie almal het dieselfde geleef nie
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Kingdom of Mapungubwe': 'a stone-walled residence likely occupied by the principal councillor'; 'Important men maintained prestigious homes on the outskirts of the capital'; a tiered hierarchy with district leaders below the capital.

items.bewering: Die gewone mense was boere en beeswagters.
items.blok: Nie almal het dieselfde geleef nie
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Mapungubwe': millet, sorghum and cotton found in storage huts; cattle, sheep and goats herded, with cattle especially important. The Met essay: commoners lived at the foot of the hill and on the surrounding plateau.

items.bewering: Handwerkers onder hulle het potte uit klei gemaak en met yster gewerk.
items.blok: Nie almal het dieselfde geleef nie
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Mapungubwe': clay pottery made in quantity, and iron mined and worked locally by smiths. SAHO, 'Mapungubwe': excavations found iron artefacts and pottery. Wikipedia notes that copper and gold work was reserved for high-status men; the lesson names only clay and iron for the craftspeople among the ordinary people, so it does not conflict with that.

items.bewering: Die mense van die dorp het dus in duidelike sosiale klasse geleef.
items.blok: Nie almal het dieselfde geleef nie
items.bron: SAHO, 'Mapungubwe': the civilisation 'was class-based'. Huffman, J. Anthropological Archaeology 28 (2009): rank-based society at K2 developed into class distinction at Mapungubwe. The Met essay calls it a class-based society.

items.bewering: Waaraan 'n mens die verskil kon sien: waar 'n mens gewoon het; watter soort voorwerpe 'n mens besit het; hoe 'n mens begrawe is.
items.blok: Waaraan 'n mens die verskil kon sien
items.bron: The Met essay: 'The homes, diet, and elaborate burials of the wealthy and privileged elite, contrast to those of the commoners, who lived at the foot of Mapungubwe and the surrounding plateau.' SAHO, 'Mapungubwe': a royal burial held gold and glass beads.

items.bewering: Hoe 'n mens se woning gebou is. Navorsers verskil oor wat die bouwyse wys.
items.blok: Waaraan 'n mens die verskil kon sien
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Kingdom of Mapungubwe': the stone walls 'served a symbolic purpose in the separation of elites and commoners' but 'possibly also served a defensive purpose'. Huffman reads elite architecture as the 'Zimbabwe Pattern'. Chirikure et al. 2014 (PLoS ONE) dispute that pattern's origin and how it should be read. The statement that researchers differ is accurate, and the lesson rightly does not take a side.

items.bewering: In die kleiner nedersettings van die vallei het mense meer dieselfde geleef. Hulle huise en besittings het minder verskil as by Mapungubwe. In die dorp kon 'n mens sien dat party mense meer gehad het as ander.
items.bron: Huffman, J. Anthropological Archaeology 2009 (via the Zimbabwe Field Guide summary): the shift from ranked society at K2 to class society at Mapungubwe changed how settlements were laid out, and rulers set themselves apart from commoners. The Met essay contrasts elite and commoner homes and burials. The comparative wording ('meer dieselfde', 'minder verskil') is correctly modest. It does not say the smaller settlements had no differences, which would be wrong, because district centres had their own leaders.

items.bewering: Sulke klasse was iets nuuts vir die mense van hierdie vallei.
items.bron: Huffman 2009: 'Rank-based society at K2 evolved into a class distinction at Mapungubwe'. Chirikure et al. 2014 (PLoS ONE) found class distinction earlier at Mapela Hill, about 90 km north-west in south-western Zimbabwe. A UCT thesis on Mapela (House, open.uct.ac.za/handle/11427/20527) places that site outside the Middle Limpopo valley. Limited to 'hierdie vallei', the claim holds. It would NOT hold if widened to 'in Suider-Afrika', and a reviser must not widen it.

items.bewering: Niemand in die dorp het neergeskryf hoe die mense daar geleef het nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Kingdom of Mapungubwe' (as summarised in search): most of what is known about the society rests on building remains, because the people of Mapungubwe left no written record. SAHO, 'Mapungubwe': all knowledge of the site comes from excavation.

items.bewering: Argeoloë het bo-op en onderaan die heuwel in die grond gegrawe. Hulle het gekyk waar voorwerpe gelê het. Bo-op die heuwel het hulle ander soorte voorwerpe gevind as onderaan.
items.bron: The Met essay: excavations found a court at the bottom of the hill and an elite graveyard at the top. SAHO, 'Mapungubwe': hilltop excavations recovered gold, iron, pottery and glass beads. Wikipedia: a cemetery of 23 graves found in the 1930s near the palace.

items.bewering: So kon hulle aflei dat mense van 'n hoër klas bo gewoon het. In die grafte kon hulle sien dat nie almal op dieselfde manier begrawe is nie.
items.bron: The Met essay: elite separated spatially on the hill, with elaborate elite burials that contrast with commoner burials. Wikipedia: 'Elites within the kingdom were buried in hills.' SAHO: a royal burial with gold.

items.bewering: dorp: 'n Groot nedersetting waar nie almal self hulle kos verbou of diere aanhou nie.
items.bron: This matches how archaeology defines an urban or town settlement: a large population with people who do not produce their own food (specialists and elite supported by others). Wikipedia, 'Kingdom of Mapungubwe' links full-time specialists to the population growth. 'Nie almal' is a properly limited quantifier, and the definition fits the lesson's own block 'Wat 'n dorp anders maak'.

items.bewering: sosiale klas: 'n Groep mense met dieselfde plek in die samelewing. Sulke groepe staan bo en onder mekaar en nie net langs mekaar nie.
items.bron: A standard sociological definition (a social class is a stratum in a ranked order). The spatial picture 'bo en onder mekaar' for a hierarchy is conventional, and its mapping holds: higher and lower rank. At Mapungubwe the physical height of the hill happens to match it. A learner could take 'bo' literally, but the lesson's own text ('So kon hulle aflei dat mense van 'n hoër klas bo gewoon het') presents the physical position as EVIDENCE that was inferred, not as the definition, so the image does not mislead. Huffman 2009 and the Met essay support the hierarchy at Mapungubwe.

items.bewering: nedersetting: 'n Nedersetting is 'n plek waar 'n groep mense saam woon.
items.bron: This is the ordinary meaning in geography and archaeology (settlement: a place where people live together). It is consistent with the term as used in the Wikipedia and Met sources above. It is accurate at Grade 6 level.

items.bewering: handwerker: Iemand wat met eie hande dinge maak, soos potte of ystergereedskap.
items.bron: This is the ordinary meaning (an artisan or craftsperson). The examples match the Mapungubwe evidence for pottery and ironworking in World History Encyclopedia, 'Mapungubwe'.

items.bewering: argeoloog: 'n Argeoloog ondersoek die dinge wat mense lank gelede gemaak, gebruik en agtergelaat het om te leer hoe hulle geleef het, en grawe is een van die maniere om daardie dinge te vind.
items.bron: This is the standard definition (archaeology studies the human past through material remains, and excavation is one method among several, alongside survey and the analysis of finds). The Mapungubwe work described in SAHO and the Met essay fits it.

opsomming: All 25 claims checked out, so the verdict is GOEDGEKEUR. Two wordings are true only because they are narrow, and must not be widened in revision. 'Een van die eerste dorpe' must not become 'die eerste': Mapela Hill in Zimbabwe shows walls and class distinction about two centuries earlier. 'Iets nuuts vir die mense van hierdie vallei' must not become 'in Suider-Afrika', for the same reason.
